observations_non_blocking: Deep link lost on return: middleware emits an ABSOLUTE callbackUrl (http://localhost:18118/dashboard) but pages/login.tsx only honors RELATIVE callbackUrl (must start with '/', not '//'), so post-auth destination always falls back to /dashboard. The user cannot return to the deep-linked page after sign-in. Minor usability gap; suggested repair is one bounded change so the middleware-emitted callbackUrl survives the existing guard (source-bound hint, ownership: Agent 1 user journey / Agent 2 auth-state per directive row 'Setup and ordinary account use').

Stale-shell window: with an expired cookie present, /dashboard renders its shell for ~6s while its data calls 401 before the interceptor bounces to /login. Single transition, no loop; user sees a briefly broken page. Minor UX polish, not a blocker.

Sign-out leaves non-auth localStorage metadata (atom_user_role, atom_chat_session_id, nextauth.message, atom_explicit_logout). Auth material is cleared; this is hygiene, not a security gap at the tested boundary.

Contract facts at this source (context for the lead): ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES is hard-coded 24h (core/auth.py:58-59); POST /api/auth/refresh requires a still-valid token, so an expired session cannot be renewed server-side; the revocation denylist is in-memory per process (restart clears it); main_api_app.py:1653 still documents a stale '15-minute expiry' comment.
